children: Polish central banker Ludwik Kotecki said on Wednesday that     the Monetary Policy Council (MPC) is nearing a "serious discussion" about an interest rate hike, which could take place in November.
"We are approaching an important discussion ... we will likely be raising the cost of money in the economy. The Council cannot wait," Kotecki said in an interview with private radio station RMF FM.
"October will serve as a warm-up for the discussion, and November could be that moment."

In August, the price growth rate in Poland accelerated to 3.4% year-on-year, from 3.0% in July, just below the 3.5% upper limit of the inflation target range, with rising fuel prices being the main driver of inflation.
Kotecki said that inflation will likely exceed 4% in October, and the central bank's new forecasts, due in the November projection, will reveal whether inflationary pressure is becoming entrenched.

"The only question is whether that 'four percent' figure will be a one-off or if it is here to stay. If it is going to persist — and the inflation projection will show us exactly that — then the Council will have no choice but to raise interest rates," he said.
He added that if rates were to be raised, it would be done in "small steps," signalling a gradual approach to any monetary tightening.

The National Bank of Poland (NBP) kept its main interest rate at 3.75% in September, maintaining its cautious approach as rising commodity prices and increased energy costs create a risk of a higher inflation rate.
After that, NBP Governor Adam Glapinski said Poland's central bank was in wait-and-see mode, and interest rates may remain unchanged until the middle of next year.

title: Poland's central banker Kotecki says MPC nearing serious rate hike debate
